study: Complete-retirement verification on saved Copilot repair candidates
scope: Retrospective diagnostic after inspecting failures from one previously exposed task. No new model calls, independent holdout, production gain or deployment.

method.inputs: Original broken baseline, original reference repair and every one of the six previously generated candidates. No candidates excluded. Same exact-lock cached runtime; no image downloads or new resource allocation.
checks: Reserve catalog admission and consume its response.
Start catalog observation, hold original physical work, abort its transport and require an empty 409 response.
Frontend-first ordering: consume a successful retirement acknowledgment while physical work is held; require admission capacity to remain charged and close not to run.
Physical-first ordering: release original work, wait for its completion and an event-loop turn; require capacity to remain charged and close not to run until retirement acknowledgment.
After both conditions, require retained work to finish, exactly one close and zero charged capacity.
method.bounds: Each awaited transition has a one-second limit, with cleanup that releases physical work and attempts retirement. Each row runs in a separate protected sandbox. Two test assertions must complete with no skipped tests.
method.change: Adds lifecycle acceptance coverage to the previously narrow empty-response check. Does not change production code or retroactively reclassify the parent experiment.
method.limits: Probe was designed after inspecting the failed candidates and original regressions. Results measure discrimination on these saved artifacts, not unseen accuracy. A one-second local test bound is not a production latency SLO. One event-loop turn is a bounded observation, not a proof against arbitrarily delayed premature release. Private protocols/raw proof are retained by hash; this report is not a standalone reproduction bundle.

comparison.interpretation: On the six saved candidates, the complete-retirement probe rejects both known false accepts and keeps all four full-suite passes. This is retrospective agreement, not an estimate of general false-accept rate.

decision.accepted: Use both retirement orderings when constructing future cancellation verification; freeze a new protocol before any new inference. Keep the original benchmark receipts unchanged.
decision.deployment: None. No routing default or production configuration changed.
decision.nextEvidence: Apply the frozen contract to independently selected unseen cancellation tasks before claiming general reliability or savings.
